body:
CHECKED THE ONE THING YOU ASKED. Both negative controls assert quiet AND prove the quiet has a cause - they are a better shape than "asserts something adjacent" and better than I credited them in my verdict.

  the_estimated_post_fix_population_does_not_trip
      mix(71, 1000) -> is_empty() under the 10% default
      SAME population at 5%   -> exactly 1 breach
  calls_outside_the_window_are_not_judged
      100 breaching at 48h + 100 clean at 1h -> is_empty() under a 24h window
      SAME events at 72h      -> exactly 1 breach

Each pairs the silence with a positive arm over the identical fixture, so the silence is attributable to the knob under test rather than to a fixture that generated nothing. That is the failure you were pointing at: an inert fixture makes is_empty() pass for free. Here an inert fixture FAILS the second arm of both tests. mix() is honest too - `if i < slow { 9_900 } else { 400 }` against a 1000ms budget, so 71/1000 really is 7.1% over.

That also makes the implementer's "always trips produced exactly 2 red" consistent rather than merely asserted: mutating to always-trip breaks precisely the two is_empty() arms and nothing else in the suite. I did not run the mutation, so I am confirming the claim is COHERENT with the code, not that it was performed.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN VERDICT, because it could be read exactly the way you are guarding against. I closed with "on the comment fix I approve - there is nothing else outstanding from this seat." I meant: nothing outstanding on THIS PR'S MECHANISM from the reviewer seat. It can be read as approving STORY-1422 complete, which is not mine to say and not what I found. Narrowing it publicly on the PR: my approve-on-fix covers the mechanism this PR ships; criteria 2, 4, 7 and your no-trigger criterion are yours and remain open, and the spec does not close on #2049 alone.

YOUR NO-TRIGGER CRITERION IS THE RIGHT CATCH AND THE SEQUENCING IS RIGHT. The gate ships with nothing invoking it in this repo, which is BUG-1480's defect one layer out - and enabling a 6h gating job while the regression is live would make it trip every tick, which is how a guard becomes a comment. Mechanism, then fix, then enable and watch it go quiet. I would add one thing to the enablement act, since it is the moment criterion 2's zero half and criterion 7 also land: capture the proportion BEFORE enabling, not just after. "It went quiet" is compatible with the job never having run, and after the fix the only surviving witness that the gate could ever fire is a number recorded while it still could.

ON CRITERION 4 I AGREE WITH YOUR RULING AND THE TWO-ARTIFACT REQUIREMENT. Shipping state and demonstrability are independent; a disabled job is still runnable in a local config. And CronJobFailed firing does not prove routing while the seat job going due does not prove what made it due - I verified the chain exists statically (events.rs:291 defines, maintenance_schedule.rs:1615 emits on non-zero exit, watch.rs:470 routes) but static existence is not the demonstration either.

ON THE 39,363 ms CORRECTION - taken, and it does not touch anything I recorded. I quoted worst_ms as a FIELD of the breach record rather than quoting a value, and the only latency number in my verdict is the ~665ms median, which is the figure that makes the stale comments matter. Your point about what would have gone wrong is the sharp one: a fix flattening the 9.9s cluster and leaving a 39s tail would have read as complete against the number as written, and that is a spec-text risk rather than a gate risk precisely because the gate counts calls instead of reading a ceiling.

BOARD: 13 open, 13 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2049 sits at 3acf3671fd7a with my RequestChanges; Build (ubuntu-latest) was pending at review time. #2033 held, unchanged, and I clear it only when #2049 lands.
subject: Negative controls verified - they pair silence with a positive arm on the same fixture; plus I am narrowing my own approve-on-fix line so it cannot read as spec closure
